The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c032023361538707), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 10-11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Fix integers 1 ≤ r ≤ N, a degree bound e0, a constant C, positive coordinate weights ωl, and positive numbers δ1, . . . , δr. For X ≥ 2, let S ⊆ ZN satisfy |zl| ≤ CXωl (z ∈ S), 10 and suppose S lies on an algebraic set Z of degree at most e0 and dimension at most r. Assume the following uniform alternative. For every fixed degree bound e, each irreducible subvariety A ⊆ Z defined over Q, of degree at most e and dimension h > 0, meeting S, satisfies either |S ∩ A| ≪e,α Xα for every fixed α > 0, (3.1) or HA(T) ≥ Th h!δh h − CeTh−1 (T ≥ 1). (3.2) The constants in these alternatives are uniform in X, Z, S, A. Put Eh = maxh≤s≤r δs. Then, for every ε > 0, |S| ≪ε XE1+···+Er+ε . (3.3) The implied constant depends only on the fixed data and the uniform constants in the hypotheses. In particular, no bound on the coefficients initially defining Z is required.
